title: Ketumpscut / Catumb Reef
summary: Ketumpscut is a Fishers Island-area placename connected with Catumb Reef, now identified as Catumb Rocks in the reef complex east of Fishers Island. Catumb and Ketumpscut are cross-referenced names for the same rocky offshore place.
address_label: Catumb Rocks / Catumb Reef, reef complex east of Fishers Island between Sugar Reef and Lords Passage
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general reef point from modern Catumb Rocks/Catumb Reef geographic-name data, used to orient Tooker's Catumb/Ketumpscut cross-reference at the east end of Fishers Island; not an exact historical boundary.
translation_content:
Ketumpscut has been interpreted as meaning "at the great rock," with the form keht-ompsk-ut. The interpretation fits the rocky reef association but should still be read cautiously against J. Hammond Trumbull's original text.

Why Place Names Matter

“It is important for students to recognize that place names are cultural creations, both in terms of how they are determined and what the names themselves reveal.”

— Montana Historical Society, Land of Many Stories (n.d.), Education guide, overview section
land_loss_content: Ketumpscut and Catumb show how Native placenames extended across islands, reefs, and navigation features, not only settled places on land. The cross-reference also shows how later writers could misplace a name, making careful source reading important.
whereintheworld_content: Ketumpscut is associated with Catumb Reef or Catumb Rocks east of Fishers Island. The exact offshore feature intended by the historic name remains uncertain.
